parts: Is there a vein from the ring finger to the heart?
Aulus Gellius, in the second century, quotes a writer named Apion.
In a history of Egypt, Apion wrote of a fine nerve from that finger to the heart.
We found no Egyptian text that says this.
The Latin name, Vena amoris, is much younger.
The earliest user we found is an English lawyer, Henry Swinburne.
His book was printed in sixteen eighty-six, after his death.
Today, an anatomy teaching site is plain: no single vein links one finger straight to the heart.
The vein of love is a myth.
